title: The Password (Chas McIvor)
style: jazz lounge piano bar dry wit spoken word observational 102bpm upright bass brushed snare deadpan baritone male vocal life philosophy absurdist technology
lyrics:
[Verse 1]
The password requires a capital letter and a number and a symbol
And at least twelve characters and something that's impossible
To guess — and also something that you'll remember — that's the brief
The password creates the problem it was meant to give relief

[Pre-Chorus]
I have written forty-seven passwords in a notebook since ninety-nine
Which defeats the security model — I know that — I'm fine

[Chorus]
The password knows something I don't know
It knows that security is just inconvenience at full flow
The password has to change every ninety days
And every ninety days I start the whole process and the haze
That's my boy

[Verse 2]
The forgotten password option sends a link that's good for ten minutes
And ten minutes is not always enough to find the phone within it
Then verify the email and then set the new one — then forget
The new one in approximately forty-eight hours — that's the net

[Bridge]
Before passwords there were keys and before keys there was trust
The password is the technological equivalent of rust
In the relationship between a person and a service
The password says I don't believe you — that's the surface

[Outro]
Password knows… we're all locked out of something… password knows
That's my boy
